slices.focus: Establishing who Colleen is and what matters to her in advance of future conversations.
slices.summary: Colleen Sweeney introduces herself fully: 36-year-old ISFJ history grad, education manager at Fireman's Hall Museum, single, lives in a South Philadelphia rowhouse. She shares her Museum Education Expansion goal, family constellation (parents Patricia/Michael, nephew Owen, executive director Leonard, volunteer Franklin, friend Nina), salary context ($52K + freelance tours), Philadelphia identity, and preferences (alternative rock, tomato pie, Phillies, detective novels, short Northeast train trips).
open_loops: Museum Education Expansion goal still aspirational -- needs to move from vision to execution plan
Voice hoarseness mentioned as seasonal issue, not yet addressed systematically
Freelance walking tours as financial cushion but unpredictable

slices.focus: Colleen uses hard data to convince Leonard to approve a formal rebuild year for the school program.
slices.summary: Colleen presents a homemade spreadsheet to Leonard showing missed capacity, weak repeat-teacher patterns, and volunteer-dependent tour length inconsistency. He approves treating 2025 as a formal rebuild year. She defines three levers: disciplined booking data, direct teacher outreach, and a revised school tour structure. Feels discouraged by the weak season but more focused now that stagnation is documented.
open_loops: Teacher outreach list needs to be built -- template not yet drafted
Revised school-tour format not yet designed, volunteer pushback anticipated
Spring scorecard defined (one tracker, teacher list, one on-time visit) but not yet executed
